blogs.title: Why Orthogonal Finetuning Matters: Preserving Knowledge in Large Models
blogs.description: An easy‑to‑understand overview of the core idea behind Orthogonal Finetuning (OFT). We'll explain how orthogonal transformations keep the angles between neurons unchanged, why that helps retain pretrained knowledge, and how this contrasts with popular methods like LoRA and adapters.

blogs.title: From Block‑Diagonal to Butterfly: Making Orthogonal Finetuning Parameter‑Efficient
blogs.description: A deep dive into the bottleneck of traditional OFT—its huge number of trainable parameters—and how the authors re‑imagined the problem as an information‑transmission task. We'll walk through the intuition behind butterfly graphs, sparse matrix factorization, and why this reduces parameters from O(d²) to O(d log d).

blogs.title: The Mathematics Behind BOFT: Orthogonal Butterflies Explained
blogs.description: A math‑focused post that breaks down the butterfly factorization, Cayley parameterization, and theorems proving BOFT’s greater expressivity over block‑diagonal OFT. Perfect for readers who want to see the formulas demystified with simple diagrams and step‑by‑step examples.

blogs.title: Putting BOFT to the Test: Real‑World Results on Vision, Language, and Diffusion Models
blogs.description: A summary of the extensive experiments from the paper, showcasing how BOFT outperforms LoRA, adapters, and standard OFT across vision transformers, large language models, and text‑to‑image diffusion models. We'll translate the tables into bite‑size takeaways and discuss what this means for practitioners.

blogs.title: Practical Guide: How to Implement Orthogonal Butterfly Finetuning in Your Projects
blogs.description: Step‑by‑step tutorial on adding BOFT to popular libraries (PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers). Includes code snippets for initializing the butterfly components, applying multiplicative dropout, and merging the learned orthogonal matrix back into the pretrained model for zero inference overhead.
